chunks: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed, those who did the evil deeds will not be requited except according to what they used to do.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward for good deeds versus punishment for bad deeds in the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-An'am establishes the foundational principle of divine justice (Adl), emphasizing that God's reward for good deeds is multiplied (often interpreted as tenfold or more in Shia exegesis), while punishment for evil is exact and proportional. It highlights the asymmetry in divine generosity versus strict retribution, assuring believers that no good deed is lost and no evil deed is overlooked. This concept is central to Shia theological discussions on the balance between God's mercy and His justice in the afterlife.
